text: Jaffle Shop's raw data is dbt Labs' own real jaffle_shop sample dataset: raw_customers, raw_orders, and raw_payments. This lesson loads all three the way a real production source lands in Snowflake.

First, a named file format describing the CSV shape, and an internal stage — Snowflake-managed storage loaded from a local machine, rather than an external stage pointed at someone else's cloud bucket.
PUT stages all three local CSV files, compressing them to gz by default. LIST confirms the stage actually has files in it before COPY INTO is asked to do anything with them.

COPY INTO loads each staged file into its target table using the named file format. Re-running the same COPY INTO a second time reports every file already loaded and loads zero new rows — Snowflake's load metadata doing its job.
All three tables land in the RAW schema specifically — nothing downstream reads from anywhere else as the landing point for new data. Next: structuring the DEV and PROD schemas on top of it.
